subject: Intermittent streaming chat lag — immediate mitigations and goodwill credit offer
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finpay.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Livechat streaming lag observed (Nov 15, 09:10-09:20 PT)

Hey Sean,

We started seeing heavy lag in our live chat flows this morning between ~09:10–09:20 PT. The UI shows long pauses during streaming responses — tokens arriving in bursts rather than smoothly. This affected about 18% of user sessions for that 10m window; we attached a short trace and the client config we were using.

Impact: some users timed out on our side, leading to degraded conversion on the payments flow. We rolled a fallback to non-streaming poll mode at 09:25 and the experience returned to normal.

Can you confirm whether there was a platform incident in our region? If not, any immediate client-side mitigations we should make to avoid this in the next peak window? We’re also tracking this with internal on-call (JIRA FPINC-4123).

Thanks,
Alice
Sr. SRE — FinPay

Attachments:
- streaming-sample-trace.txt (log excerpt, 12KB)
- client-config-snippet.json (client opts)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming lag observed (Nov 15, 09:10-09:20 PT)

Alice — thanks for the quick trace and the config snippet. We’re looking into telemetry now. Initial notes / quick mitigations you can apply immediately: 

1) Temporary client fallback: keep the non-streaming poll fallback as your primary for the next 24 hours if that preserves the UX; polling is more resilient to microburst token delays.

2) Short-term client tweaks (no deploy needed for most SDKs): reduce the per-turn max_tokens from 1024 -> 512 and lower the response chunk buffer to 128 bytes — this reduces server-side emission granularity and KV cache strain.

3) Connection keepalives / read timeout: increase client read timeout to 45s and add a 1s jittered reconnect for stream resumes.

4) Model fallback: if you can tolerate slight quality change for latency-sensitive endpoints, switch from rdx-large-v2 (streaming) -> rdx-medium-v1 (streaming) for affected routes; we can pre-warm the medium instance for you.

We’ve opened internal FPINC-4123 and looping in CS (Marissa) and SE (Hannah) to coordinate a follow-up RCA and remediation plan. I’ll confirm whether there was any server-side throttling or autoscaler activity in your region once I have SRE logs.

Short-term, I’m going to provision a warm pool on rdx-medium-v1 in your us-west region (can revert once cleared). Standby for a cross-functional update in ~60–90 minutes.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming lag observed (Nov 15, 09:10-09:20 PT)

Hi Alice — quick update from Ops + proposed customer-facing mitigations and goodwill gesture: 

Summary of what we did in the first 60m:
- Provisioned a warm pool of rdx-medium-v1 in us-west and routed 30% of your streaming traffic there as a safety net.
- Identified a short microburst pattern in the token emission pipeline at 09:11–09:17 PT caused by a transient spike in batching at the edge proxy; no persisted throttles.
- No data exposure, no PII concerns; this is performance-only.

Customer guidance (recommended order):
- Keep your non-streaming fallback in place for the next 24 hours.
- Apply the temporary client tweaks Sean listed (max_tokens and buffer). We can provide a pre-built snippet for your SDK if you prefer.
- If you want to retain streaming but avoid UI jitter, route lower-priority customers to rdx-medium-v1 while premium users stay on rdx-large-v2. We’ll set up routing rules for you.

Operational next steps & timeline: 
- Today EOD (Pacific) — final SRE log package and initial post-incident timeline.
- Tomorrow noon PT — RCA draft with remediation tickets and estimated ETA for a permanent fix (kernel/batching smoothing change).

Goodwill credit: to compensate for the impact to conversions, we’re prepared to apply a one‑time usage credit equal to 25% of your hosted streaming charges for Nov 15 (applied to your next invoice). If you’d like a different offset (flat credit or extended trial), let us know.

I’ve attached the short trace you provided and a link to a client-snippet we can push as a patchless mitigation.

—Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- client-config-snippet.json (suggested non-breaking adjustments)
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finpay.com, jordan.lee@finpay.com
Date: 2026-11-16T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming lag observed (Nov 15, 09:10-09:20 PT)

Marissa / Sean — thanks for the quick triage and the credit offer. We accepted the temporary routing to rdx-medium-v1 and applied the client tweaks; the streaming UI is smooth during today’s morning peak.

Please proceed with the RCA draft and include the specific kernel-level change you reference — we’d like to understand whether this needs a coordinated deploy on our side (client changes) or is purely server-side. Also please confirm the credit amount and how it will appear on our Nov invoice (FP-2025-09-87).

Appreciate the fast help — Alice
Sr. SRE, FinPay
